The Registry retired step-up requests. Token creation is now browser-only and a CLI credential receives browser_session_required with the settings URL. Token revocation still takes authority away without an extra verification challenge.

The Registry no longer issues step-up requests or accepts their evidence for CLI writes. Browser-only actions refuse a CLI credential with browser_session_required and name the web settings page. Device sign-in and publication authorization retain their separate flows.

There is no Registry step-up request for an unattended CLI write to resume. Browser-only actions return a web settings destination; device sign-in and publication authorization continue to own their distinct resumable handoffs.

Publishing requires a session or a token, so there is no signed-out publish approval left to resume. The obligation described the browser-approved publish capability end to end: the saved initiator proof, the exact-inputs recheck before exchange, and the one-time polling exchange. Every part of it went with the capability. The separate Registry step-up challenge was retired later.
